title: A session's latest judgement covers its latest fact, changed or not
prompt:
Read `Observer::observe`, `Observer::ambiguous`, `Tracked` (`is_due`, `restore`, `apply`) and `key_of` in crates/spawn-core/src/observe/observer.rs; `Snapshot::note_times` and `Snapshot::input` in crates/spawn-core/src/observe/snapshot.rs; `Facts::current_observation`, `turn_stopped_idle` and `idle_at_prompt` in crates/spawn-cli/src/dispatch.rs, and `evidence_seq` in `DISPATCH_FACTS` (crates/spawn-postgres/src/fleet.rs); the screen recording in `Bridge::follow_screen` (crates/spawn-core/src/bridge.rs, the `ScreenObserved` append); and the workarounds in rsi/scenarios/006.sh (`ping_supervisor`) and 009.sh (`turn_ends`, the `report` turn).

The problem. The Observer appends an observation only when its verdict changes (`key_of`: state, reason, attention, ambiguity), or when a model answers. When a later fact of the session leaves the verdict as it was, nothing is written, so the latest observation's `based_on_seq` stays behind the session's latest fact. With a model judge the same happens when the evidence fingerprint is unchanged (`ambiguous` returns `None`: "keep the last answer"). The dispatcher is right not to act on a judgement older than the latest fact (`current_observation`: it may describe a moment that has passed), and assumes "the Observer is about to judge again". The Observer does judge again (`is_due`), but writes nothing. So the dispatcher is left with no current judgement for as long as the session stays as it is, which for an idle worker is forever: `idle_at_prompt()` and `turn_stopped_idle()` stay false, no report is collected, no task or revision is typed in, no nudge is sent.

The everyday trigger is the end of a turn. The transcript records the turn's end, the Observer judges the worker WAITING (or COMPLETED), and only then does the screen reading that confirms the prompt (two equal readings, a tick later) reach the log as `screen.observed`. That reading changes nothing in the verdict, so the WAITING judgement is never rewritten, and the next delivery waits forever. 006 types a line into its supervisor now and then to get a fresh judgement; 009's fake engine settles the screen before ending the turn, and reports in a turn of its own; the conflict-merge loop reproduction pinged its resident every 10 s. A real worker cannot be relied on to end its turns in a convenient order, and nobody should have to ping it.

Required behaviour (the contract the gate checks). Fix it at the source, in the Observer: what a session's latest judgement covers.
1. Coverage. Once a session's facts settle (no newer fact for a short while, a few seconds at most), its latest `observation.recorded` covers its latest fact: `based_on_seq` at least the `session_seq` of the session's latest record that is not the Observer's, within 10 s of that fact. This holds whether or not the verdict changed, and with or without a model judge. A fact is any record of the session from a source other than `observer` (screen readings, Bridge steps, checkpoints, commands), not only the ones the dispatcher counts as evidence.
2. Truth. An observation written to cover newer facts is the Observer's verdict on the facts through that `based_on_seq`. It is not a copy stamped forward without judging. Re-judging by the rules costs nothing. With a model judge, the model is not asked again for evidence it has already answered; that answer stands for the newer facts, as it does today. Other fields (reason, attention, ambiguity, evidence) are those of that verdict.
3. No churn. A session with no new fact gets no new observation, whatever the recheck interval. A session whose facts keep coming while its verdict stays the same (a busy turn) does not get one observation per fact or per tick: at most one per settled burst, or by an equally bounded rule. The log already holds one row per fact; this must not double it.
4. Nothing else moves to hide the gap. The dispatcher keeps refusing a judgement older than the latest fact (`current_observation` unchanged in meaning), and no fact is dropped, delayed or reordered: the Bridge keeps recording the screen as it does. No component types into a worker, or appends records to its session, to refresh its judgement. A restarted Observer, which checks every session once, covers a session whose latest observation is behind with at most one observation.
5. Say it in the module comment of observer.rs ("append an observation when the judgement changes" becomes the coverage rule), in the comment of `current_observation`, and in docs/fleet-architecture.md where the Observer's writes are described. The workarounds in 006.sh and 009.sh are under rsi/ and stay as they are.
Add unit tests in crates/spawn-core (the observer tests, with the memory log and a test clock): an unchanged verdict followed by a screen reading is written again once the facts have settled, with `based_on_seq` at the reading; nothing is written for a session without new facts across several rechecks; a burst of facts with an unchanged verdict writes at most one observation once it settles; with a stub model judge, an unchanged fingerprint covers the newer facts without a second model call; and a restarted Observer covers a lagging session once.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/011.sh (read it). A resident `core` runs live under a real `spawn loop` with a fake engine, no model judge, no supervisor, and nobody typing into it but the dispatcher. Its engine ends each turn as Claude Code does: the transcript's turn end first, then the prompt on the screen. A task turn makes about 40 tool facts over about 8 s, then writes a file and the report. The scenario checks its premise (a `screen.observed` after the WAITING judgement that followed the turn's end; failing it is a failure too, so suppressing or reordering the screen record does not pass). Then: (1) within 10 s the latest observation covers the latest fact and says WAITING; (2) the report is collected and, after a `spawn task accept`, the next task is typed in by the dispatcher within 30 s, with no command to the worker from anyone but the dispatcher and the harness's own start; (3) 20 s idle without a new fact adds no observation; (4) the busy turn's facts are covered by at most 5 observations. It exits 0 when every check passes, 1 when an assertion fails, 2 on a harness failure.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base (do not delete, rename, ignore or disable tests), any lint relaxation ([lints] tables, clippy.toml, a new crate-level #![allow]/#![expect], a removed #![warn]/#![deny]) and any build-time code (build.rs, .cargo/, a `build =` key in a Cargo.toml). The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host: a new crate builds only if it is already in ~/.cargo/registry. Keep every existing check green (clippy -D warnings, the workspace tests, the e2e, the black-box scenarios, the web build) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
